problems.title: Mechanism identification: a pre-registered statistic that separates reaction-diffusion from colonisation, phase separation and buckling on static patterns
problems.gap: Pattern phenomenology does not identify mechanism: zebrafish stripes are cell-contact mediated (Nakamasu 2009), feather buds mechanical first (Shyer 2017), Holstein spotting indistinguishable between growing RD and Eden colonisation at p=0.91 (OP-11). No registered discriminator exists that, given only an adult pattern, says which class of generator made it with a stated error rate.
problems.done: A hash-locked discriminator (candidate features: radial power-spectrum shape, Minkowski functionals, defect/junction statistics, two-point anisotropy) trained and scored on synthetic ground truth from four generators (Gray-Scott/Schnakenberg RD, Eden colonisation, Cahn-Hilliard phase separation, elastic buckling) with a pre-registered held-out accuracy threshold and published confusion matrix; then applied blind to the 10 coat-masked Holstein specimens, reported either way.
problems.tool_route: models/1981-murray-bos-taurus-turing-wavelength.py (RD + Eden generators, coat masks, paired harness); models/1952-turing-morpho.py (Pearson classes); morphoeval/measure_outputs.py; predictions/ registry for the hash lock. Cahn-Hilliard and buckling generators must be written fresh (the catalog *_morphogen_condensation / *_elastic_buckling scripts are alpha-template scaffolds, scout-048).
problems.deciding_data: In repo: 10 Holstein masks, RD/Eden outputs. Synthetic ground truth generated in-run. No wet data needed.
problems.prior_attempts: OP-11 (static Turing rejected; growing RD vs Eden p=0.91) is the direct precursor; scout-040 OP-11 Delphi rescore pending.
problems.hypothesis: A pre-registered multi-feature discriminator reaches its registered held-out accuracy on synthetic four-generator ground truth AND returns a definite class for the Holstein set.

problems.title: The diffusion-ratio problem: which molecularly identified Turing systems can be two-species at all?
problems.gap: Two-species activator-inhibitor models need D_inh/D_act above the Lean-checked threshold (d_c = 3.93 for the repo's Gray-Scott Jacobian; ~4-10 generally), yet measured extracellular diffusivities rarely show it; three-node networks with an immobile node remove the requirement (Marcon 2016) and extracellular wiring changes behaviour qualitatively (2025 bioRxiv). Nobody has tabulated, system by system, which of the molecularly supported cases (WNT/DKK, FGF/Shh palate, Bmp-Sox9-Wnt digits, GDF5/NOG joints, EDAR/WNT/BMP ridges, Nodal/Lefty) actually satisfies the two-species condition with measured D.
problems.done: A registered table of >=6 molecular Turing systems giving measured or bounded D_act, D_inh (with DOI), run through the repo's dispersion relation, classifying each as two-node-feasible / needs immobile third node / D unmeasured; the count in each class pre-registered before the literature values are looked up.
problems.tool_route: python3 morphoeval/scout_literature.py --query '<morphogen> diffusion coefficient FRAP FCS' per system; models/1952-turing-morpho.py dispersion (Lean turing_differential_diffusion_instability, d_c = 3.9271); predictions/ registry row for the pre-registered counts.
problems.deciding_data: Public literature only. Known in hand: Nodal/Lefty D measured (Mueller 2012); GDF5/NOG model needs no differential diffusion (Grall 2024). Others likely unmeasured — that is itself the finding.
problems.prior_attempts: None in repo. scout-063 ZF-TUR-01 kernel-checked a size-prior D ratio (D_inh/D_act < 1 for chd/bmp2b) — a related negative.
problems.hypothesis: The census reaches a classification for >=6 systems, with the pre-registered class counts scored, and at least one system falls in each of the three classes.

problems.title: The fine-tuning objection: replicate the two-node vs three-node Turing parameter-volume ratio and the 1%-uncertainty retention claim
problems.gap: Turing instability is topologically common but occupies tiny parameter volumes: 0.00035% of sampled space for the classical two-node circuit vs 0.022% for the best three-node topology (Tica et al. 2024, Latin-hypercube linear stability), with 33% retention under 1% parameter uncertainty around a Turing I point. These numbers decide whether the fine-tuning objection to biological Turing systems stands; they have not been independently reproduced.
problems.done: A pre-registered Latin-hypercube linear-stability sweep on the repo's two-node kinetics and a three-node immobile-node topology within published parameter bounds, reporting both Turing fractions and the 1%/5% local-retention fractions; verdict = within one order of magnitude of the published ratio (>=10x three-node over two-node) or not.
problems.tool_route: models/1952-turing-morpho.py (Jacobian / dispersion code, Pearson Saddle-Node & Hopf curves, Lean d_c); new sweep script under morphoeval/ or models/; registry row for the ratio before running.
problems.deciding_data: Published fractions (Tica 2024 Fig. 2A, Table S5 bounds; Scholes 2019 atlas) — no biological data needed.
problems.prior_attempts: scout-034 proposed a 12-class Pearson (F,k) sweep, not a robustness fraction; nothing recorded on parameter volume.
problems.hypothesis: The repo's sweep reproduces the published two-node vs three-node Turing-fraction ratio within one order of magnitude and the >=10x ordering, with the pre-registered numbers scored.

problems.title: Growing domains: an independent ontogenetic stripe-count series to test the insertion law blind
problems.gap: Classical Turing conditions are neither necessary nor sufficient on growing domains and wavelength selection under growth has no closed theory (Krause et al. 2021). Empirically, Kondo-Asai's Pomacanthus series remains nearly the only ontogenetic stripe-count dataset, and the repo's Kondo stripe table is calibrated on it (circularity recorded in scout-034/038; OP-06 growing-domain solver debt still open).
problems.done: A hash-locked prediction N_stripes(L) = round(L/lambda_c) with lambda_c fixed from one stage, scored on an independently sourced Pomacanthus (or other stripe-inserting fish) ontogenetic series of >=6 stages with body length metadata, each image SHA-256 pinned before counting; result reported either way.
problems.tool_route: python3 morphoeval/scout_literature.py --taxon 'Pomacanthus semicirculatus' (Commons + OpenAlex); verify_image_fitness.py / the Y-junction skeleton detector for counting; predictions/ registry for the lock.
problems.deciding_data: Not in repo. Needs public juvenile photographs with size metadata or a published series other than Kondo-Asai 1995 Fig. 1.
problems.prior_attempts: scout-031 (Kondo ontogenetic series beyond one adult photo), scout-034/038 (circular calibration), scout-032 (Y-junction over-count) — all record the gap, none closed it.
problems.hypothesis: An independent >=6-stage series with size metadata is found and the locked insertion-law prediction is scored decisively (all stages within +-1 stripe, or not).

problems.title: Scaling: does biological pattern wavelength scale with body size across taxa, against Turing's intrinsic wavelength?
problems.gap: Turing wavelength is set by kinetics and diffusion, not domain size, yet many biological patterns scale with the organism (planarian regeneration, Werner 2015; expansion-repression schemes). No cross-taxon regression of measured wavelength against body size exists. The repo's 976 *_turing_wavelength dataset folders look like such an asset but their empirical_series are alpha-template curves (x_control 0.5-5.0, r=0.999 fits), not measurements (scout-048 / scout-062 data-quality findings), so they cannot decide this.
problems.done: A pre-registered log-log regression of measured pattern wavelength on body size for >=10 taxa with real, DOI-cited measurements (hair-follicle spacing, fish stripe period, digit spacing, palatal ruga spacing), slope and CI locked before extraction; verdict = slope CI excludes 0 (scaling) or excludes 1 (intrinsic) or neither.
problems.tool_route: scout_literature.py for measurements; a new extraction table under datasets/; registry row. The catalog templates must NOT be used as evidence.
problems.deciding_data: Not usable in repo (template artefacts). Public literature extraction required.
problems.prior_attempts: scout-048 BIO-TPL-DQ-01 and scout-062 established the catalog empirical curves are template artefacts; no scaling test attempted.
problems.hypothesis: A >=10-taxon measured wavelength-vs-size table is assembled and the locked slope test returns a decisive class.

problems.title: Reproducible topology: why five digits every time when RD from noise gives defective labyrinths
problems.gap: RD from random initial conditions yields labyrinths with defects; embryos give five digits almost every time. The Turing + positional-information hybrid (Hox dosage sets wavelength, FGF/Wnt gradients orient) explains cases, but there is no general, tested account of how prepattern and boundaries lock topology.
problems.done: A Bmp-Sox9-Wnt three-node RD on a growing fan-shaped limb-bud domain with published parameters and gradient modulation, pre-registered to produce exactly five rays in >=95% of 200 random-IC runs (and the Hox-dose polydactyly series of Sheth 2012 on dose reduction); scored as registered.
problems.tool_route: New script (no BSW model exists in models/); 2D RD solver base from models/1952-turing-morpho.py; registry row for the 95% threshold.
problems.deciding_data: Published parameters (Raspopovic 2014 SOM). No wet data.
problems.hypothesis: A faithful BSW growing-domain model reproduces five rays in >=95% of random-IC runs and the Hox-dose polydactyly ordering.

problems.title: When does continuous reaction-diffusion collapse to a discrete automaton? Meinhardt mantle PDE vs the Lean-proved Rule 30 gate
problems.gap: Ocellated lizard scales behave as a cellular automaton emerging from RD on a thick-skin lattice (Manukyan 2017), and the repo has Lean-proved that the Ermentrout-Oster neural mantle gate is bit-for-bit Rule 30 — but whether the repo's Meinhardt-Klingler Conus PDE, discretised at the mantle, induces a Rule 30-class local rule has never been measured. It is the bridge between the Rule 30 programme and the RD programme, and the RD-vs-neural shell-pattern debate is still molecularly unresolved.
problems.done: From a Meinhardt PDE kymograph at the mantle edge, extract the empirical 3-neighbourhood -> next-state transducer table (binary threshold pre-registered), report the fraction of transitions agreeing with Rule 30 vs Rule 90 vs best-fit rule, plus the 2D ANF-carry density and wall chirality already used to separate R30 from R90 (node r0); verdict thresholds locked before running.
problems.tool_route: models/1984-wolfram-conus-textile-rule30.py (Meinhardt-Klingler PDE + Rule 30 + kymograph); morphoeval/lean/ Ermentrout-Oster gate theorem; measure_outputs.py for ANF carry / chirality; registry row.
problems.deciding_data: All in repo (PDE, CA, Lean gate, 2D observables).
problems.prior_attempts: scout-003 (Rule30 <-> Ermentrout-Oster gate chain traceability); scout-034/038/039 (stochastic activator injection debt, OP-06b). None extracted the transducer table.
problems.hypothesis: The extracted transducer table from the Meinhardt mantle PDE agrees with Rule 30 above the locked threshold on both 1D transitions and 2D ANF/chirality observables.

problems.title: Synthetic realisation: a robust, deterministic periodic Turing pattern in eukaryotic cells
problems.gap: Bacterial three-node circuits now give reproducible concentric stripes but remain condition-sensitive (Tica 2024); the mammalian Nodal-Lefty circuit most likely produced solitary, not periodic, patterns (Sekine 2018). A robust eukaryotic periodic Turing pattern has not been built.
problems.done: Wet-lab: a eukaryotic circuit producing periodic patterns with pre-registered wavelength reproducibility across >=3 biological replicates. The repo can only contribute the Turing-vs-solitary regime map of the published circuit model.
problems.tool_route: None adequate: no wet lab. Modelling satellite only (regime map of the Sekine competitive-inhibition model).
problems.hypothesis: This repo brings the synthetic eukaryotic Turing problem to a decisive verdict.

problems.anchor: Turing 1952 Sec. 10 (oscillatory case) -> Ca2+ wave-vector pipeline
problems.title: Turing's neglected case: is there a wave (Turing-Hopf) dispersion signature in the embryonic Ca2+ wave field?
problems.gap: Turing 1952 also derived oscillatory, travelling-wave instabilities; essentially no developmental system has been shown to use one. The repo's Ca2+ spark-track data (x, y, t per event) is the only place here that can ask whether an observed wave field carries a dispersion ridge omega(k) distinct from a single driven front (omega = v k).
problems.done: A pre-registered space-time spectral test on existing spark_tracks CSVs: estimate the (k, omega) power surface per embryo, fit the driven-front line, and test for a secondary ridge against phase-randomised surrogates at a locked false-positive rate; report per-embryo outcomes and the pooled verdict either way.
problems.tool_route: wave-vector-analysis/ (spark_tracks.csv schema, embryo_units.py for em/s conversion); new spectral script; predictions/ registry for the surrogate threshold.
problems.deciding_data: In repo: wave-vector-analysis/test_data/spark_tracks_qc_folder31.csv, _folder33.csv and analysis_results/*.csv; orientation and coordinate caveats recorded (COORDINATE_SYSTEM_WARNING.md, OP-07).
problems.prior_attempts: scout-036 proposed binned AP spark spectra vs Turing k_c and a travelling-front vs static-labyrinth gate; neither run. Blind tests OP-07/08 found orientation, not wave features, carried signal.
problems.hypothesis: The registered surrogate test returns a decisive per-embryo verdict (secondary ridge present/absent at the locked rate) on the in-repo spark-track data.

problems.title: Ecology-scale Turing: fairy circles as scale-dependent-feedback RD vs termite engineering
problems.gap: Namibian and Australian fairy circles are still contested between vegetation reaction-diffusion (scale-dependent feedback) and termite engineering; Tarnita 2017 shows the two are not exclusive. Pattern statistics alone (hexagonal order, pair correlation) have not settled it — the same lesson as TOP-01.
problems.done: A pre-registered comparison of a vegetation RD model and a termite-territory model against public aerial-imagery pair-correlation and Voronoi statistics with locked discrimination thresholds; reported either way.
problems.tool_route: No ecological model or imagery in repo; new scripts and a public data fetch would be required.
problems.deciding_data: Public aerial imagery / published point patterns (Getzin et al.). Nothing in repo.
problems.hypothesis: Pattern statistics from public imagery decisively favour one mechanism at the locked thresholds.
